subject: PathWare MAP: unit-cost clarity for pilot evaluation and close timeline
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@pathware.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Romero <alex.romero@pathware.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T16:10:00Z
Subject: PathWare MAP: unit-cost clarity for pilot

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement wants the MAP to include clear unit economics for the pilot so they can sign off: tokens/$ assumptions, expected caching hit rates, batching behavior for our traffic profile (avg len ~280 tokens, 1.2 calls/user/day), and fallback model costs.

Can you provide a short evaluation plan + an explicit cost checklist we can put in the MAP? We'd like the MAP to reflect anything that could materially change cost vs the initial quote.

I'll loop procurement if you need docs. Targeting a pilot start 2026-12-07 — is that still reasonable on your side?

Thanks,
Nina Patel
VP Product, PathWare
PathWare | nina.patel@pathware.com

[attachment: RFP_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@pathware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Alex Romero <alex.romero@pathware.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: PathWare MAP: unit-cost clarity for pilot

Hi Nina — great to hear. Yes, pilot start 2026-12-07 is achievable if we lock the evaluation milestones this week. Attached is a concise evaluation plan and the cost checklist we use for MAPs. High-level items we’ll include in the MAP: 

- Baseline token assumptions: avg request tokens (prompt+response) and 95th pct length, tokens per embedding/dedup if used.
- Batching profile: expected QPS, per-request latency target, and batching window (we recommend 5–15ms for low-latency apps; can be increased for higher throughput).
- Caching/KV assumptions: prefix reuse rate and expected hit rate; we’ll run a short trace to estimate effective hit.
- Fallback model policy: cost delta between primary and fallback variants and expected fallback frequency.
- Monitoring hooks: token-level breakdown, per-route cost, and gating thresholds for MAP acceptance.

I attached a starter spreadsheet (PW_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a 1-page econ summary. Ben will follow up with a preliminary per-token unit math using your sample payloads.

If procurement needs a dedicated security/compliance section now, we can drop it in — otherwise we'll include the standard SOC2/KMS addendum link in the MAP.

Next steps: Ben and I will produce a short worksheet with conservative and optimistic token/$ scenarios by 11/23. We'll also ask you for a 3-day traffic capture (anonymized) to run caching simulations.

Best,
Logan Wright
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-econ-summary.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@pathware.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: PathWare MAP: unit-cost clarity for pilot — preliminary econ workbook

Hi team — attaching the workbook with two tabs: 'Assumptions' and 'Scenarios'. Key items called out in the sheet and in-line here: 

- Unit math basis: we assume 1 token = billing unit. Primary model is rw-medium-22b (baseline price $0.00012 / token). Fallback cheap variant rw-small quantized ~ $0.00003/token.
- Average tokens per call: conservative = 420, expected = 300, optimistic = 210 (these include prompt+response).
- Caching hit rate: we treat prefix caching as adjustable. Sim runs: 0% / 20% / 45% hit. Note: domain-specific prompts show higher reuse; our sim uses a 3-day sample you provided (thank you).
- Batching window: we modeled 5ms, 25ms, and 100ms windows. For PathWare’s target latency < 200ms, 25ms batching yields ~1.6x throughput efficiency.
- Effective tokens/$: under expected baseline (300 tokens, 20% cache, 25ms batching) our model shows $0.0108 per user/day (1.2 calls/user/day) and $3.24 per MAU/month.

Risks to call out in the MAP (things that materially change cost):
- Response length growth (e.g., adding context >1.5x tokens)
- Low cacheability for certain workflows (hit rate <10%)
- Unanticipated retrains or larger model switch during pilot

I've added detailed row-level calcs in PW_MAP_v2.xlsx and a small samples file (pw_perf_samples.jsonl) showing the token distributions we used. Please review and flag any assumption you think is off and we'll re-run.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[attachment: PW_MAP_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

1) For the MAP acceptance gate, can you provide a simple acceptance rule we can add to the contract? (e.g., actual cost per MAU in first 30 days <= 1.2x quoted scenario).
2) Do we have a firm fallback SLA when the primary model is unavailable? We need the cost and latency impact documented.
3) Can you confirm whether embeddings or reranking are priced separately or included in your tokens/$?

Also, a small ask: procurement would like a signed Statement of Work (SOW) with the MAP appended before commit. They can provide a template — should I loop our procurement contact or send it to a shared DocuSign?

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@pathware.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: PathWare MAP: unit-cost clarity for pilot — final checklist & timeline

Nina — thanks for the procurement questions, answered inline below. I've also updated the MAP checklist and added a short acceptance clause you can paste into the SOW. See below and attached DocuSign link.

1) MAP acceptance gate (suggested clause to place in SOW):
"MAP Acceptance: During the first 30 calendar days of the Pilot, actual average cost per MAU (calculated as total billed tokens divided by average MAU in that period) shall not exceed 1.25x the Quoted Scenario shown in the MAP workbook. If the threshold is exceeded due to causes within Redwood's control (e.g., model serving regressions, billing misconfiguration), Redwood will provide a remediation plan and apply a pro-rated credit for the excess cost. If exceeded due to product changes requested by PathWare (e.g., longer context windows), the parties will document and approve an updated MAP."

2) Fallback SLA and impact: Primary model fallback will be configured with automatic routing to rw-small-quantized under capacity pressure; expected latency increase +30–60ms and per-token cost delta as shown in the workbook. Fallback frequency will be monitored and surfaced on the MAP dashboard.

3) Embeddings/reranking pricing: Embeddings are priced per embedding call as listed in the MAP workbook (separate line item). Reranking (if performed server-side by Redwood) is charged under the same token model; if PathWare runs client-side reranking using embeddings we can provide the embeddings-only pricing.

DocuSign: here's a link to a draft SOW with the MAP attached — you can route through procurement: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/PW-4721-MAP. If procurement prefers, they can send a template to contracts@redwood.com; we’ll populate and return within 48 hours.

Next steps and timeline: 
- 11/30: Finalize MAP workbook after PathWare confirms any changes to average token lengths.
- 12/01–12/03: Redwood runs caching simulation on 3-day trace and produces detailed hit-rate report.
- 12/07: Pilot begins. Monitoring and MAP dashboard live.

If that looks good I'll mark the MAP as ready-to-sign and ping contracts for the SOW.

Best,
Logan Wright
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | logan@redwood.com
